doc.title: Håkan Rydin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016

title: What he thinks about when improvising
summary: Playing best when not thinking: flow, concentration with relaxation, and responding to the band.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Okay last — here’s a very easy question to wrap up. What do you think about when you improvise?

Yes. Very easy. How many hours do we have? I guess — I think you play best when you don’t think. But it’s not easy to say that. And you can’t say now I’m not going to think. But if that’s some state of mind, some feeling that every jazz musician knows when you have flow when things are happening and you could just do things maybe you haven’t done before and things like that. At that moment you don’t think. But some people call it a peak experience or something. And maybe in a whole concert it happens once or even it sometimes doesn’t happen. Sometimes if you are lucky you can have many peaks of experience, and you try to reach that but it’s not so easy of course, it’s very difficult to reach them. I think it’s two things going on. You have to be concentrated and you have to be relaxed. And those are — if you’re concentrated you might be too concentrated, and if you are too relaxed you make mistakes. So it’s relaxed and concentrated, and it’s very difficult. But if you can maximize both of them I think you have a good possibility of playing good. And then you don’t think that much. But of course you think and you’ve got some idea of what to play. I can get influenced by what’s happening before. So if I play with a saxophone player and he played eight choruses of really groovy things, maybe I’ll try to play soft, or very little. I mean that’s a deliberate choice at that moment, but it wasn’t decided before. If you think things are a little unstable in the band I try to play very simple, I try to make it swing. If I think nothing is happening I try to put some energy into it and do some counter-rhythm or something like that. So it depends on what’s happening and what’s happened before. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
That was an excellent answer to a tough question.
